title: The Year of Long Knives
teaser: Hitler purges his own movement while Mao begins his march into legend. Totalitarianism codifies itself — in Berlin, in Moscow, in Hollywood. Yet Paris publishes Tropic of Cancer, Max Ernst collages nightmares, and a young philosopher in Vienna asks how we know what's true.

art.label: Art
art.content: Max Ernst publishes Une semaine de bonté (A Week of Kindness), 182 collages assembled in three weeks from Victorian engravings — bird-headed men, lion-bodied women, floods and earthquakes rendered with nightmare precision. This is Surrealism's graphic masterpiece: Ernst slices the 19th century's respectable illustrations into nightmares of desire and violence, each day governed by an element (mud, blood, darkness). In Leni Riefenstahl, art serves opposite masters: she films the September Nuremberg Rally with revolutionary techniques — sweeping crane shots, heroic low angles, synchronized editing to Wagner — transforming political spectacle into cinema. Triumph of the Will (released 1935) will become totalitarian aesthetics' defining monument, demonstrating that avant-garde technique serves power as easily as it subverts it.

lit.label: Literature
lit.content: Henry Miller's Tropic of Cancer appears in September from the Obelisk Press in Paris — a book so sexually explicit that U.S. Customs immediately bans it (until 1961). Miller's plotless, ecstatic prose destroys the boundary between autobiography and fiction, between obscenity and philosophy. F. Scott Fitzgerald publishes Tender Is the Night, his portrait of American expatriate dissolution, while Robert Graves gives antiquity a cynical modern voice in I, Claudius. Samuel Beckett's first prose collection More Pricks Than Kicks appears, already pared toward the void. Meanwhile, in Moscow the First Congress of Soviet Writers formally adopts Socialist Realism as mandatory doctrine: art must be "national in form, socialist in content" — the bureaucratic murder of the avant-garde.

phil.label: Philosophy
phil.content: Karl Popper publishes Logik der Forschung (The Logic of Scientific Discovery) through the Vienna Circle, though he critiques their logical positivism from within. His central claim: science advances not through verification but falsification — a theory is scientific only if it specifies what would disprove it. The Vienna Circle debates verification while fascism rises outside their seminar rooms. In Barmen, Germany, theologian Karl Barth drafts the Barmen Declaration (May 31), rejecting the Nazi-aligned "German Christians" movement: "Jesus Christ, as he is attested for us in Holy Scripture, is the one Word of God" — theology as political resistance, faith refusing to be nationalized.

hist.label: History
hist.content: On June 30, the Night of the Long Knives begins: Hitler orders the SS to murder the SA leadership, including Ernst Röhm, along with conservative rivals and old enemies. At least 85 people die in three days — extrajudicial murder dressed as national salvation. On August 2, President Hindenburg dies; Hitler merges the offices of Chancellor and President, becoming Führer. The Wehrmacht swears personal loyalty oaths to Hitler, not to Germany. In October, Mao Zedong's Communists begin the Long March — a 6,000-mile retreat from Nationalist forces that will forge the myth of revolutionary endurance and establish Mao's leadership. In Hollywood, the Hays Code is strictly enforced from July 1: cinema censors sex, violence, and moral ambiguity. Three systems of control crystallize simultaneously.

conn.label: Connections
conn.content: The year maps the border between freedom and control. The same avant-garde techniques that Ernst uses to expose bourgeois nightmares — collage, montage, fragmented imagery — Riefenstahl deploys to glorify fascist spectacle. Both are modernist methods; their politics diverge completely. Miller's Tropic of Cancer appears in Paris precisely because Paris still permits what New York, Berlin, and Moscow forbid — the year's geography of censorship is also a map of where thought remains possible. Popper's falsificationism, written as the Vienna Circle debates, will outlast logical positivism itself, becoming science's self-understanding — but Popper will soon flee Vienna as the world his philosophy describes collapses into ideological warfare.
conn.funFact: The Hays Code banned showing husband and wife in the same bed on screen — while Tropic of Cancer, published the same year, describes sex with a frankness American readers wouldn't legally encounter for another 27 years.
